title: Fruit Salad
strapline: Wash it, chop it, share it out — a safe, colourful first taste of cooking for the littlest hands.
intent: Young children take part in real food preparation that is safe and manageable for them — washing, peeling, mashing, mixing.
Children explore fruit with every sense — colour, smell, texture, taste — and build a willingness to try new things.
Children use early cutting and spreading tools with support, developing hand control.
Children meet early maths naturally — one each, more, all gone, sorting by colour.
Children learn where fruit comes from and enjoy the sociable pleasure of sharing food.
implementation: Offer soft, safe fruits to prepare — banana, strawberry, melon, orange — with child-safe knives and plenty of supervision.
Let children wash, peel a banana, pull grapes (halved by an adult), mash and stir themselves.
Name colours, smells and textures as you go, and invite tasting without pressure.
Weave in gentle maths — 'one strawberry each', 'more melon?', 'all gone!', sorting the pieces by colour.
Model and support the tools — a child-safe knife on a soft banana, a spoon to stir the bowl.
Keep it truly hands-on and low-numbers so every little one has a real job.
Talk about where the fruit grows and share the salad together at snack.
key_questions: What colour is this fruit — and how does it smell?
Shall we give everyone one piece each?
How does the banana feel when you squish it?
Would you like to try a little taste?
Which fruit is your favourite in our bowl?

impact.text: Children take part in safe, real food preparation — washing, peeling, mashing, mixing.
Children explore fruit with all their senses and grow willing to try new tastes.
Children use early tools — spoons, child-safe knives — with support and growing control.
Children meet early maths — one each, more, all gone — and sort fruit by colour.
Children learn where fruit comes from and enjoy sharing food together.
Children feed themselves and notice hunger, enjoying what they've helped make.

enhancements: Soft, safe fruits — banana, strawberry, melon, orange — ready to prepare.
Child-safe knives, spoons and a mashing bowl.
A washing station with a bowl and jug for rinsing the fruit.
Small bowls and forks so everyone gets their own portion.
A colour chart to sort the fruit pieces onto.
Aprons and a simple handwashing song before cooking.
Pictures of the fruit growing on trees and plants.

playing_exploring: Little ones explore fruit with hands, nose and tongue.
They test squishing, stirring and tasting to see what each fruit does.
active_learning: Children concentrate hard on peeling the banana or mashing the berry.
Helping make the snack and then eating it is a whole, satisfying loop.
creating_thinking: Children choose which fruit to add and notice colours and smells.
They begin to link the fruit in the bowl to the fruit that grows on trees.
